ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus, with points $E$ and $F$ on sides $AD$ and $CD$ respectively, and $AE=CF$, $BA=BE$. If $\angle EBF=30^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Let the measure of $\angle C$ be $x$, thus $\angle A=\angle C=x$,\\
in $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle CBF$,\\
since $\left\{\begin{array}{l}BA=BC\\ \angle A=\angle C\\ AE=CF\end{array}\right.$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ABE\cong \triangle CBF$ (SAS),\\
therefore $\angle ABE=\angle CBF=180^\circ-2x$,\\
thus $\angle ABC=2\left(180^\circ-2x\right)+30^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ABC=\angle D$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC+\angle D+\angle A+\angle C=360^\circ$,\\
that is: $2\left[2\left(180^\circ-2x\right)+30^\circ\right]+2x=360^\circ$,\\
solving gives: $x=\boxed{70^\circ}$,\\
thus, the measure of $\angle C$ is: $70^\circ$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is drawn as a rhombus in a diamond shape, with A on the left, B below, C on the right, and D above. Point E is located on side AD, and point F is located on side CD; BE, BF, and EF are connected in the figure, where BE and BF form the angle ∠EBF=30° given by the problem at point B. Reasoning: Let ∠C=x. Because ABCD is a rhombus, it is a parallelogram, so ∠A=∠C=x, and BA=BC. Compare △ABE and △CBF: BA=BC, AE=CF, and the included angles ∠A=∠C, so △ABE≅△CBF (SAS). Also because the problem gives BA=BE, △ABE is an isosceles triangle, with base angles ∠BAE=∠AEB=x, therefore ∠ABE=180°−2x. From congruence, ∠CBF=∠ABE=180°−2x. According to the order of the rays at point B in the figure, ∠ABC=∠ABE+∠EBF+∠FBC=(180°−2x)+30°+(180°−2x)=390°−4x. Adjacent angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so ∠ABC=180°−x. Thus 180°−x=390°−4x, solving gives 3x=210°, x=70°. Therefore ∠C=70°.
